content.value_statement: New Firebase projects often miss emulator setup, security rules, and architecture decisions. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured Firebase project setup workflow.
actual_capabilities: Guides Firebase CLI verification, login, project directory creation, and Firebase initialization steps.
Collects hosting, authentication, functions, and security model choices before scaffolding.
Defines emulator UI settings and verification checks for local Firebase development.
Outlines TypeScript Cloud Functions structures for Express, domain grouped, or individual function layouts.
Prompts setup for Firestore rules, Vitest tests, Biome linting, and initial commits.
limitations: It does not create Firebase resources without agent or user action.
It does not include the referenced example documentation files in this package view.
It does not validate cloud IAM, billing, or production deployment settings.
It does not manage secrets beyond recommending local environment files and gitignore entries.

use_cases.title: Start a Product Prototype
use_cases.description: Create a Firebase project with emulators, TypeScript functions, hosting, rules, and tests from the first setup session.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Firebase Setup
use_cases.description: Use a repeatable checklist for architecture choices, local emulators, linting, and verification before feature development starts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Client Project Foundations
use_cases.description: Document hosting, authentication, functions, and security decisions while creating a maintainable Firebase starter structure.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to initialize a new Firebase project. Ask me the required architecture questions before creating files.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Local Development
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Firebase emulators, TypeScript functions, Vitest, and Biome for a new project. Include a verification checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Functions Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Express API, domain grouped functions, and individual function files for this Firebase app.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Setup Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete Firebase setup plan with hosting, auth, functions, security rules, emulator workflow, tests, and first commit steps.

output_examples.input: Initialize a Firebase app for a small web product.
output_examples.output: A guided setup checklist covering CLI login, project creation, hosting choice, authentication approach, functions layout, rules, emulators, tests, and linting.

output_examples.input: Help my team pick the right Firebase functions structure.
output_examples.output: A comparison of Express API, domain grouped functions, and individual functions, followed by the recommended project structure.

output_examples.input: Prepare local Firebase development before feature work starts.
output_examples.output: An emulator-first workflow with verification steps for build, lint, tests, emulator UI access, environment files, and documented architecture decisions.

best_practices: Answer the four architecture questions before generating files or running setup commands.
Keep environment files local and confirm they are ignored by version control.
Run emulator, build, lint, and test checks before considering the setup complete.
anti_patterns: Skipping emulator setup and testing until after features are built.
Copying production secrets into prompts or shared setup notes.
Selecting client-write security rules without documenting the risk and rule strategy.

faq.question: Does this skill run Firebase commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflow steps. The agent or user must still decide which commands to run in the workspace.

faq.question: Can it set up Cloud Functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides TypeScript Cloud Functions setup and offers Express, domain grouped, and individual file structures.

faq.question: Does it support multiple hosting sites?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks for hosting configuration and includes single site, multi-site, and target-based hosting choices.

faq.question: How does it handle secrets?
faq.answer: It recommends local environment files and gitignore entries. Users should not share production secrets in prompts.

faq.question: Is it only for new projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for new Firebase projects, not debugging or adding features to existing apps.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
